skill.name: Dialogue that moves the story on
skill.why: Every line of talk should push the story forward, not just fill space.
skill.how: Cut the hellos. Keep lines that reveal something, cause trouble or make a choice.

beats.say: Some talk just fills space. Nothing happens.

beats.show: '**I've seen Maxx's van at the jetty.**'
'**Don't tell Wren,** but I let the Creature out.'

beats.say: Or it forces someone to choose.
beats.show: '**We can save the egg or the boat. Not both.**'

beats.say: Before you keep a line, ask: what does it change?

weDo.frame: The crew is hiding behind a rock, watching Maxx's boat.
weDo.prompt: Which line of talk moves the story on?
weDo.hint: Which line changes what the crew might do next?
weDo.success: An open cage door is news. Now the crew has a chance, and the story speeds up.

options.text: 'Look, he's left the cage door open,' whispered Zed.
'Hello, Zed,' said Tully. 'Hello, Tully,' said Zed.
options.reason: They just say hello. Nothing new happens, so the story stands still.
It's chit-chat. It doesn't reveal anything or cause any trouble.

weDo.frame: Tully is cutting lines from her script for the ship's play.
weDo.prompt: Put each line in the right bin.
weDo.hint: Ask: does anything change after this line?
weDo.success: Lines that bring news, start trouble or force a choice move the story. Chit-chat just fills space.

items.text: 'The bridge is out. We'll have to swim.'
items.reason: It gives news that changes the plan.
Nothing is really said, so nothing changes.
A confession like that starts trouble straight away.
Weather chat doesn't push the story anywhere.

items.text: 'Pick one: the map or the snacks.'
items.reason: It forces a choice, and choices drive stories.
Hellos fill space but tell us nothing new.

creature.name: Natterflit
creature.blurb: A glider that chatters as it leaps from tree to tree. Each squeak carries it further, so it's never stuck on one branch.

workshop.mentor:
'Don't freak out,' said Mo, 'but the soup is moving.'
Gus leaned over the pot. Something green blinked back. 'That's not soup. That's a Creature.'
'It was soup when I started,' said Mo.
'Then where did the soup go?' asked Gus.
Mo went very quiet. Then he burped, and a tiny bubble of light floated out of his mouth.
'OK,' said Tully, grabbing the first-aid kit. 'Nobody tell Wren. And nobody, under any circumstances, tell Maxx's followers we've got a glowing chef.'
Outside, a drone buzzed past the porthole, its red light blinking.
'Too late,' whispered Zed.
workshop.ask: Write a scene that's mostly talk, where every line changes something. Ideas: the crew finds Maxx's van, a lost footy bet, a ghost on the phone.
checklist: I cut the hellos and chit-chat.
I made every line change something.
I started a new line for each new speaker.
I made it clear who is talking.
